name: Alexander Machado
headline: Simplifying EU AI Act Operationalization | Head Trustworthy AI | MLOps | TUM | CDTM | UnternehmerTUM | Max Planck Society | BMW | Bavarian Elite Network
summary:
AI is bringing immense value in multiple disciplines across the world. However, we need to ensure it is aligned with our safety, health and fundamental human rights. We at appliedAI empower companies in Europe to operationalize Trustworthy AI as a competitive advantage to drive innovation and create trust on European AI. We support companies operationalizing the EU AI Act at the organizational-level, use case-level and upskilling their workforce with AI literacy. 

If you are struggling to set up your AI Governance processes to develop AI use cases according to the EU AI Act, don't hesitate to reach out to us! 

Short Bio: Alexander Machado is the Head of the Trustworthy AI and former Head of MLOps Processes at appliedAI Initiative. He has a decade of experience in Data Science, Artificial Intelligence, and Data Engineering at appliedAI, the Max Planck Society, and BMW. His work focused on leading, planning, and developing AI solutions from experimentation to production. He has developed multiple MLOps frameworks and published an MLOps online course. Currently, he is further developing processes that address the inherent challenges of production systems and compliance with the upcoming AI Act. Background in Electrical and Communications Engineering at the Technical University of Munich and Honours Degree in Technology Management at the Center for Digital Technology and Management (LMU-TUM).

Previously: Head of MLOps Processes team at appliedAI, supported companies to efficiently reduce AI project failure rate and augment the impact of AI in their disciplines. Senior AI Engineer leading and consulting AI Projects, defining and evaluating use cases, developing AI solutions from experimentation to production, understanding technical challenges and best practices from the customers along the ML life cycle and their AI journey.

positions.title: Senior Artificial Intelligence Engineer

Developed and led multiple AI-Solutions in agile teams:

- Tender Tool (9 months): Developed and led an agile team for the upgrade and optimization of an AI-based smart bidding tool, currently used in production. Maintained internal feature store, model-data versioning system, deployment, data ingestion, data engineering, advanced analytics (counterfactuals), autoML. Analysis of medicines sales, stock and more than 100 features in every node of the supply chain, from manufacturers to the patient. Stack: Hive, Scoop, Python.

- ML Pipeline (3 months): Comparison and Evaluation of state-of-the-art AI tools for: Data Versioning, Model Versioning, Deployment, and Monitoring. Developed and applied a methodology to compare state-of-the-art tools and frameworks for different components of the ML life cycle (data versioning, experiment tracking, model versioning, deployment) per field of interest (NLP, time series, image recognition).

- Stockout detection (6 months): Designed and implemented an early stockout detector algorithm, with multivariate multi-step time series forecasting. Big data tools: Pyspark, Hive, Impala, Python. Developed an algorithm to forecast stock out of medicines in pharmacies over different periods of time, spanning from one to three months in the future. Developed both the PoC and the production code, following the company requirements for fast and scalable algorithms.

- Working Group Enterprise ML (4 months): Collected and analyzed main challenges and best practices in the ML lifecycle from sessions with appliedAI's partners. Developed appliedAI's view on the ML lifecycle based on internal and partners experiences.

- Knowledge Transfer (9 months): Led a team of 4 engineers in order to automate the information 
extraction of relevant metadata from Emails by using Natural Language Processing.

- Professionalisation Framework (3 months): Part-time developer of the appliedAI python library to support the best practices of applying AI in production.

positions.title: Master Thesis for the Master of Science in Communication Engineering - Master Thesis Patented
positions.description:
Master Thesis Title: Modelling Objective QoE and Task Performance Metrics for Automotive Video Streaming Applications.
Master Thesis Grade: 1.0
Master Thesis Patented
Publications on the Thesis: 
1.- Co-author of Conference Paper and Patent Application: “Camera context based estimation of spatial and temporal activity parameters for video quality metric in automotive applications”. At BMW, Munich, Germany.
2.- Co-author of Conference Paper and Patent Application: “Bit rate estimation for H.264/AVC video encoding based on temporal and spatial activities”. At BMW, Munich, Germany.

Description: In this work, a low complexity approach for the estimation of temporal and spatial parameters, of videos captured by a front-facing camera of a vehicle, based purely on vehicular sensor data is presented. The estimated parameters are integrated into an objective video quality metric which can be used to determine the perceptual quality of a compressed video stream. The proposed metric has very low computational complexity which makes it suitable for live video streaming applications. In addition, another novel bit rate model was developed for H.264/AVC video encoding. The model is based on the quantization parameter, the frame rate as well as temporal and spatial activity measures. With the proposed model, it is possible to trade off the frame rate versus the quantization parameter to achieve a target bit rate. Our model depends on video activity measures that can be easily calculated from the uncompressed video. In our experiments, the model achieves a PC of 0.99 and a RMSE of less than 5%.
Software: MATLAB, Microsoft Excel, LaTeX.

positions.title: Internship for the Master of Science in Communication Engineering
positions.description:
Internship Title: Edge computing and suitability of LTE for future automotive off-board services.
Description: In this work, the suitability of LTE for future automotive off-board services was investigated. A scenario with rural traffic mobility, real density of vehicles, real life applications and specific QoS assignments was simulated using the software OPNET and the results were analyzed. In addition, the feasibility of different strategies that may reduce the end-to-end delay of the communication between the BMW vehicles and a back-end server, by bringing the server to the edge was analyzed.
Software: MATLAB, OPNET.
